name: Philosophy - BA - Science, Technology, and Medicine
narrative: A major in philosophy requires a total of fifteen philosophy courses, at least twelve of which must be upper-division (courses numbered 100 and above).

Up to two upper-division courses outside of philosophy can count among the twelve required for the major if they are drawn from a related field and contribute to the major's philosophical program; such credit must be approved by the undergraduate adviser.
Honors and directed study courses (PHIL 191–199) may not be used to satisfy the major requirement of fifteen philosophy courses.

Seven of the twelve upper-division courses in the major must be taken in the Department of Philosophy at UC San Diego. Courses taken at other institutions may be applied toward the major by petition only.
All courses applied toward the major must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of C– or better. A GPA of 2.0 must be maintained in courses applied toward the major.

items.label: History of Philosophy
items.notes: These courses must be taken in order.

items.label: Upper-division philosophy courses
items.notes: At least twelve of the fifteen courses must be upper-division; the seven upper-division core courses and the four emphasis courses count toward the twelve, so one more is needed here. PHIL 191–199 may not be used. Up to two upper-division courses outside philosophy may count with adviser approval.

items.label: Remaining philosophy courses
items.notes: Fifteen philosophy courses in all; the eight core courses (PHIL 10 included), the four emphasis courses and the upper-division course above count toward the fifteen, so two more (lower- or upper-division) are needed here.

sections.name: Area of Emphasis: Science, Technology, and Medicine

requirement.label: Science, Technology, and Medicine
requirement.notes: Five emphasis courses in all; the Philosophy of Science core course (every option is on this list) counts toward the five, so four more are needed here. Students selecting an optional area of emphasis must take and pass five of the courses listed under that area. Courses taken to complete an area of emphasis are counted toward the fifteen courses required for the major and may also fulfill a core requirement. Areas of emphasis are not noted on transcripts or diplomas.
